title: Tobal No. 1
subtitle: A fighting game with room to step aside

body: Tobal No. 1 is DreamFactory's PlayStation fighting game, first released in Japan on 2 August 1996. Characters designed by Akira Toriyama compete in three-dimensional arenas, where movement around the opponent is part of the exchange. The player chooses between high, middle and low attacks, then mixes strikes with grappling and defence. Its uncluttered character designs keep those actions readable as the fighters circle one another. The game brings together an experienced fighting-game designer and an artist strongly associated with manga, giving Square an unusual entry into a genre outside its best-known role-playing games.

The ability to move through the arena makes distance and angle matter alongside the next attack. Closing in can turn an exchange of strikes into a grapple, where the relationship between the two bodies becomes the central problem. The player has to read the opponent's response and decide whether to continue the pressure or move away. Quest mode takes the fighting system into dungeon exploration, giving those same controls another purpose beyond a conventional tournament. A system learned against one rival becomes a way to navigate a longer sequence of encounters.

Seiichi Ishii directed the game after contributing to Virtua Fighter and Tekken, while Toriyama supplied its cast. A large group of Square composers worked on the soundtrack, including Yasunori Mitsuda, Yoko Shimomura and Masashi Hamauzu. Japanese and North American copies also included a sampler disc with a playable Final Fantasy VII preview, giving the release another place in PlayStation history. Tobal itself received a generally positive response and found particular success in Japan. Its sequel remained Japan-only, leaving the original as the series' principal international release.
